framework: Food-insecurity risk outlook (E69): regional hunger is the only food-insecurity outcome measured every quarter; it is combined with province evidence on affordability (price-pressure score, headline inflation) and climate (PAGASA status, local crop production). ELEVATED = hunger expected above 11.3% AND (an affordability hazard OR a climate hazard with a local production drop); WATCH = hunger expected high AND a climate hazard only. It is an evidence summary for planning, not a probability and not a validated provincial forecast; it does not change the score, colour or rank.
goalStatus: The >75% Lead-2 goal applies to province classifications and is not met on valid evidence (E68: 0.72; no correction better). For regional hunger, 'above 11.3%' at Lead-2 was right in 12/18 quarters, below always predicting 'above' (72% on the same quarters).
provinceSkill: The provincial price model separates provinces within a quarter (within-quarter AUC 0.71; 36 of 50 correct against 32 when every province gets the quarter average), so its province ordering carries information beyond the shared regional trend; the five provinces count as about 23 independent observations, not 50.

2026-Q4.evaluation: Two quarters ahead, no method forecast regional hunger better than its latest reading: average error 3.9 points over 18 quarters (survey noise alone is about 1.8); 'above 11.3%' was right in 12 of 18 quarters and none of the 4 sharp rises (5 points or more) was foreseen. SWS samples 300-600 adults in Balance Luzon (margin of error about 4-6 points) and gives no provincial figure.
2026-Q4.model: latest posted SWS reading (random walk; E69 R0)
